summary: This program defines a function that takes two pieces of information at once \u2014 a list of food and a table number \u2014 and prints out Beepo's delivery for that table. Calling it twice with different arguments shows the same function doing the same job for two different orders.

lines.text: Two parameters, separated by a comma, let the function receive two pieces of information in one call. Their order matters: whatever you pass first becomes food_list, and whatever you pass second becomes table_number.

lines.code: """Helps Beepo the robot waiter deliver food to a table."""
lines.text: A docstring sits just inside the function and states in plain words what the function is for, so anyone reading the code later knows Beepo's job without tracing the lines.
A parameter can hold any type of data, including a whole list, so the function loops through the order and prints each item in turn no matter how many dishes were sent in.
The \n adds a blank line at the end, which keeps the two deliveries visually separated when the function runs more than once.
The list is written directly inside the parentheses as the first argument and the table number as the second, matching the order of the parameters in the definition.
Calling the same function a second time with different arguments is the whole point of writing a function: one set of instructions, reused for every order Beepo takes.
